children: Goldman Sachs Research said industrials are now trading at a higher 12-month forward P/E valuation than technology, highlighting a shift in relative sector pricing, according to the firm’s latest sector valuation analysis.
The research compares MSCI World sector and style valuations with their historical ranges over the past 20 years.

Industrials currently trade at a 19.4x forward P/E, placing the sector above the broader market at 16.7x and technology at 16.2x. Industrials also rank among the more highly valued areas of the global equity market, behind only growth at 20.6x, consumer staples at 18.7x and consumer discretionary at 18.7x.

The valuation gap is notable because technology has historically commanded a premium relative to many other sectors. Goldman Sachs Research's data shows that communication services trade at 18.1x forward earnings, while health care stands at 17.7x. Utilities are valued at 15.1x, followed by materials at 14.6x and value stocks at 14.0x.

At the lower end of the valuation spectrum, energy trades at 12.8x forward earnings, while financials have the lowest multiple among the sectors shown at 12.7x. The dispersion underscores the wide differences in how global equity sectors are currently valued relative to their longer-term historical ranges.

The figures come as investors assess sector positioning amid changing expectations for interest rates, earnings growth and capital spending. Goldman Sachs Research has also noted that overall U.S. equity valuations have moderated this year, with the S&P 500's forward P/E falling from around 22x to 19x, while valuations relative to bonds have remained broadly unchanged.
